record.paper_title: Recent progress and open problems in the Bergman space
record.original_question: For an inner divisor phi in L^2_a(D), let Phi_phi be the potential associated with phi, satisfying Delta Phi_phi = |phi|^2 - 1 in D and vanishing on the boundary circle, with the boundary gradient condition used for inner divisors. The known isometry for f in H^2(D) is ||phi f||^2_L2 = ||f||^2_L2 + integral_D |f'(z)|^2 Phi_phi(z) dS(z). Determine precisely for which inner divisors phi this isometry extends to every f in L^2_a(D), allowing the value +infinity on both sides.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ be the open unit disk and let $dS$ denote normalized area measure on $\mathbb{D}$. Define the Bergman space
$$L^2_a(\mathbb{D})=\Big\{f\in\mathrm{Hol}(\mathbb{D}):\|f\|^2_{L^2_a}=\int_\mathbb{D}|f(z)|^2\,dS(z)<\infty\Big\},$$
and the Hardy space $H^2(\mathbb{D})$ of holomorphic $f$ on $\mathbb{D}$ with $\sup_{0<r<1}\int_0^{2\pi}|f(re^{i\theta})|^2\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}<\infty$.

A function $\varphi\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ is called an inner divisor (in the Bergman sense) if it has unit norm and 
$$\int_\mathbb{D} (|\varphi(z)|^2-1)\, q(z)\,dS(z)=0$$
for every bounded holomorphic $q$ in the invariant subspace generated by $\varphi$ (equivalently, $\varphi$ is the extremal/canonical divisor of its zero-based invariant subspace).

For such $\varphi$, let $\Phi_\varphi:\overline{\mathbb{D}}\to\mathbb{R}$ be the unique function satisfying
$$\Delta\Phi_\varphi(z)=|\varphi(z)|^2-1\quad\text{on }\mathbb{D},\qquad \Phi_\varphi\big|_{\partial\mathbb{D}}=0,$$
together with the natural boundary condition on the gradient appropriate for inner divisors (so that $\Phi_\varphi\ge 0$ on $\mathbb{D}$).

It is known that for every $f\in H^2(\mathbb{D})$,
$$\|\varphi f\|^2_{L^2_a(\mathbb{D})}=\|f\|^2_{L^2_a(\mathbb{D})}+\int_\mathbb{D}|f'(z)|^2\,\Phi_\varphi(z)\,dS(z). \qquad (\ast)$$

Determine precisely the class of inner divisors $\varphi\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ for which the identity $(\ast)$ extends to all $f\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$, where both sides are allowed to take the value $+\infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search returned general references on Bergman inner divisors, contractive divisors, and Hedenmalm's expansive multiplier/isometry identity, but did not yield a specific result establishing or refuting that the isometry $(\ast)$ extends to all of $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ for a characterized class of inner divisors. No publication characterizing precisely the class for which the extension holds was identified, so the status remains unclear.

status_evidence.title: Beurling's Theorem for the Bergman space
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes the inner-divisor isometry for Hardy-class multipliers but does not address full L^2_a extension.
status_evidence.claim: Original isometry stated for H^2 multipliers, with extension to broader classes left open.

status_evidence.title: Curious properties of canonical divisors in weighted Bergman spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies canonical/inner divisors and their curious behavior in weighted Bergman spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature on inner divisors does not appear to settle the L^2_a extension of the isometry.
